models.name: users
models.description:
Users - This implements user entity requirement from 5.2 'User' and 6.1/6.2 business rules. 

Holds all platform participants' credentials, role, and account status. For example, it enables registration/login, tracks who can create threads/comments, and supports moderation login.

Key relationships: One-to-one with user_profiles. Linked to threads, comments, votes, and moderation_actions by foreign keys. Role/ban status directly impacts allowed actions.
Special behaviors: Only registered users can post or vote. Enforces unique username/email.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each user.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description:
Username - Implements unique account login/lookup. 
Stored as unique display handle. For example, login as username123. Unique across all users.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
User email - Implements contact/account linking. 
Email address for registration and password resets. Unique; required to prevent duplicate accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description:
Encrypted password - Implements security and compliance requirement. 
Hash of user password for secure storage. Example: bcrypt hash string. Not readable in UI.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description:
Display name - Implements user identity for display purposes. 
Shown on threads/comments. Example: 'Jane Doe'. Updatable by user.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description:
Account role - Implements RBAC as described in 6.1. 
User's system role: guest, user, moderator, admin. Example: 'user'. Controls permissions.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Account status - Implements rule for active/suspended/banned/locked accounts. 
Shows if user can post or is locked/banned. E.g. 'active', 'suspended', 'banned'.

plainFields.name: registered_at
plainFields.description:
Registration date/time - Implements auditing and compliance. 
Timestamp for account creation.

models.name: user_profiles
models.description:
User profiles - This implements requirement for extended profile from 5.2 and supports profile management for each user (optional fields). 

For display & personalization (bio, avatar, etc.). Example: user can edit their profile bio. One-to-one with users.

Key relationships: Foreign key to users. Each profile connects back to a user.
Special behaviors: Each user has at most one profile (enforced by unique user_id).

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user's {@link users.id} - Links profile to user.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description:
Profile bio - Implements user personalization feature. 
Optional free-text about user. Example: short biography or interests.

plainFields.name: avatar_url
plainFields.description:
Profile image URL - Implements user personalization. 
User's avatar picture URI. Optional, can be null if not set.

models.name: categories
models.description:
Categories - This implements requirement for content grouping from 5.2/6.1. 

Defines thread grouping for search/filter. For example: category='Economics' or 'Foreign Policy'.

Key relationships: Linked to threads (many-to-many via junction table if needed).
Special behaviors: Category/translatability support by name/description. Name must be unique.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Category name - Implements content grouping/organization. 
For search and filter. Example: 'Economics'. Unique.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Category description - Implements discoverability. 
Longer description/metadata for the category. For user help or UI tooltip. Optional.

models.name: threads
models.description:
Threads - Implements requirement for main discussion objects (see 5.2, 6.2, 4.1/4.2/4.6). 

Core discussion topic started by a user, with title, content, timestamps, status, category, and author link. For example: user creates thread 'Impact of Sanctions on Global Economy'.

Key relationships: Many-to-one with user (author), many-to-many with category, one-to-many to comments.
Special behaviors: Title must be unique within category (enforced by index).

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: Author's {@link users.id} - Links thread to user who created it.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Category's {@link categories.id} - Assigns thread to a category.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description:
Thread title - Implements main discussion summary for display/search. 
Example: 'Debate: Market Regulation'. Required, indexed.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description:
Thread content - Implements main post body. 
Full text of thread starting post. Supports rich text. Required.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Thread status - Implements open/closed flag for posting. 
E.g. 'open', 'closed'. Default 'open'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Created timestamp - Supports audit and search. 
Time of thread creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Last update timestamp - Implements evidence/storage for most current version. 
Updated on thread edit.

models.name: comments
models.description:
Comments - Implements comment and threaded reply structure (see 5.2, 6.2, 4.2, 5.3). 

Represents both direct replies to threads and nested replies to comments. For example: a user responds to a thread, or replies to another user's comment (nested).

Key relationships: Foreign keys to thread, author, and parent comment (nullable, for nesting). Many-to-one to both thread and author; self-reference for nested replies.
Special behaviors: Parent_id can be null for top-level; non-null for replies. Displays thread and parent linkage.

foreignFields.name: thread_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged thread's {@link threads.id} - Links comment to thread.

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged user's {@link users.id} - Creator of comment.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment's {@link comments.id} - Enables nesting of replies to a comment. Null if top-level reply.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description:
Comment content - Implements reply body. 
Full text of comment/reply. For example: "I agree with your point.". Required.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Comment status - Implements active/removed/hidden flag. 
E.g. 'active', 'removed'. For moderation/audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Created timestamp - Implements modification/audit trail. 
Comment creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Updated timestamp - Implements audit trail/history. 
Time of last edit.

models.name: votes
models.description:
Votes - Implements upvote/downvote requirement (see 4.5, 5.2). Optional, but included for full traceability and audit.

Tracks user's voting actions (single vote per user per item). For example: user upvotes thread #42. Can reference either thread or comment.

Key relationships: User_id, optional foreign keys to thread or comment (must be only one per row – model enforces with nullable, app must check).
Special behaviors: Only one vote per user per target. Type is up or down. Votes on comments or threads; both targets optional but only one NOT null.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Voter's {@link users.id} - Identifies which user cast the vote.

foreignFields.name: thread_id
foreignFields.description: Target thread's {@link threads.id} - Nullable, vote target may be a thread.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: Target comment's {@link comments.id} - Nullable, vote target may be a comment.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description:
Vote type - Implements up/down requirement. 
'up' for upvote, 'down' for downvote. Required.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Vote creation timestamp - For audit purposes and to prevent duplicate voting. 
Time vote was cast.

models.name: moderation_actions
models.description:
Moderation actions - Implements moderation tracking (see 4.4, 5.2, 6.3, 5.4). 

Logs admin actions on content or users – deletions, bans, edits, re-categorization, etc. Example: moderator bans user #99 for abuse. Used for audit, appeals, and compliance.

Key relationships: Actor foreign key (user ID, moderator/admin), target_type and target_id fields for generic target (may be user/thread/comment).
Special behaviors: Each record tracks type, reason, and before/after timestamps. Links to user being acted upon if applicable.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Performing moderator's {@link users.id} - User who did the moderation action.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description:
Target type - 'user', 'thread', or 'comment'.
Specifies moderation action's object type.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: Target object's ID - References the actual moderated record. Application checks validity.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description:
Action type - Implements the type of moderation done. 
E.g. 'ban', 'remove', 'edit', 'warn'. For audit/reporting.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description:
Reason - Implements justification requirement from business rules/audit. 
Moderator-written log as rationale. Example: 'Hate speech'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Action timestamp - Implements compliance/audit.
When the moderation action was performed.

models.name: users
models.description:
[User entity] - This implements the user account and platform access requirement from the platform core data entity specification (Section 5.2, 'User'). 

Represents individual users of the discussion board, including account credentials, role for permissions, and account status for moderation. For example, mapping a registered user's login details, registration date, permissions, and ban/suspension state. 

Key relationships: Each user can have one user_profile ({@link user_profiles}), many threads and comments ({@link threads}, {@link comments}), votes, and moderation actions performed/received. 
Special behaviors: Only registered (non-guest) users exist in this table; password is required and must be stored encrypted. Role determines system access. Account status manages active/banned/suspended accounts.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the user account.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description:
[Username/handle] - Implements the visible user identity requirement. 

A unique login name displayed throughout the platform. For example, shown with threads and comments. Must be unique platform-wide.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
[Email for account contact and recovery] - Implements user contactability and password recovery. 

For password resets, notifications. Must be unique per user. Not shown publicly.

plainFields.name: password
plainFields.description:
[Encrypted password] - Implements the secure authentication requirement. 

Passwords are securely hashed and required for login. Stored as a hash, not plaintext.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description:
[Displayed name] - Implements the user customization feature. 

Allows user to show a preferred public name. For example, for more informal or privacy-focused appearance.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description:
[User role] - Implements the role-based permissions requirement. 

One of: 'user', 'moderator', 'admin'. Determines access permissions.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
[Account status] - Implements moderation and restriction requirement. 

Status such as 'active', 'banned', or 'suspended'. For example, prevents login if banned.

plainFields.name: registered_at
plainFields.description:
[Registration timestamp] - Implements audit and join date tracking. 

Records when the user registered. For example, used for calculating tenure or ordering new users.

models.name: user_profiles
models.description:
[User profile entity] - Implements the requirement for user information extensions and personal profile. 

Stores additional details for each user, such as bio and avatar. For example, a user can describe themselves and upload a profile picture that's shown next to threads/comments. 

Key relationships: Each profile is strictly linked 1:1 with a user ({@link users.id}). 
Special behaviors: Profile is optional in content, but always exists 1:1 per user for extensibility.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the profile record.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description:
Belonged user's {@link users.id} - strict 1:1. 
Ensures the profile corresponds to one and only one user.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description:
[Biography] - User personal description. 

For example, shown on the profile page to introduce themselves. Optional; blank if not provided.

plainFields.name: avatar_url
plainFields.description:
[Profile picture URL] - Public profile image. 

Optional. If provided, visible with posts and profile.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
[Profile last updated timestamp] - For audit and change tracking. 

Indicates latest modification time. For example, used for notification of profile updates.

models.name: categories
models.description:
[Category entity] - Implements the requirement for topic hierarchy and thread organization (Section 5.2, 'Category/Tag'). 

Represents a discussion area/category, used to group threads. For example, 'Economy', 'Politics', 'News'. Enables filtering and organization of threads. 

Key relationships: Threads ({@link threads}) reference categories via foreign key. 
Special behaviors: Category names must be unique; description may be provided for user guidance.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the category.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
[Category name] - Implements unique topic area identification. 

Required, serves as group label for threads. For example, 'Tax Policy'. Must be unique across all categories.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
[Category description] - Informs about the category's topic focus. 

Optional; used for user help, onboarding, moderation guidance, etc.

models.name: threads
models.description:
Thread entity - This implements the discussion initiation requirement from the requirements analysis (Section 4.2.1, 5.2 Thread). 

Represents discussion threads created by users on political or economic topics. Each thread provides a title, main content, author, timestamps, and links to categorization. 
For example, a user posting a thread about recent economic policy would create this record.

Key relationships: Linked to users (authors), categories/tags, and a 1:N relationship to comments. Supports status (open/closed) for moderation/business-rule enforcement.
Special behaviors: Only registered users can create threads, threads are not deleted but may be marked closed/hidden by moderation, audit trail tracking via timestamps.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description:
Primary Key - Implements unique thread identity (requirement 5.2 ThreadID).

Uniquely identifies each thread. Ensures precise referencing in relationships (comments, votes, moderation actions).

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description:
Author's {@link users.id} - Implements user-thread association (requirement 5.2 Thread Author).

References the user who created the thread. For example, the account posting the discussion topic.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description:
Thread category's {@link categories.id} - Implements category organization (requirement 5.2 Thread Category).

References the primary category or tag for the thread. For example, 'Economics', 'Politics', etc.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description:
Thread title - Implements the thread title requirement (requirement 5.2 Thread Title).

Main headline for the thread topic. For example, 'Impact of New Trade Sanctions'. Must be concise and descriptive. Required and indexed for search.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description:
Thread content - Implements main content requirement (requirement 5.2 Thread Content).

Full thread body as authored by user. For example, the discussion starter's argument or question. Supports rich text formatting subject to application logic.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Thread status - Implements moderation/business rule enforcement (requirement 5.2 Thread Status).

Indicates if thread is 'open', 'closed', 'hidden', 'deleted', etc. Used for both moderation/locking and for soft-deleting threads per business rules. Required for enforcing post-participation permissions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Thread creation timestamp - Implements audit trail (requirement 5.2 Thread Timestamp).

The datetime when the thread was first posted. Required for chronological listing and legal compliance.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Thread last updated timestamp - Implements audit/history requirement (6.5 Data Integrity).

Timestamp of most recent edit. For example, tracks content updates or title changes. Required for proper chronology, audits, and displaying edit information.

models.name: thread_snapshots
models.description:
Thread snapshot entity - This implements the audit/history, evidence, and fraud-prevention requirement for thread content (drawn from best practices and BBS snapshot architecture).

Represents a versioned snapshot of a thread's content/state for every update, preserving historic changes and supporting rollback or evidence for dispute resolution. 
For example, whenever a thread is edited, a new snapshot record is created linked to this thread.

Key relationships: Linked to the parent thread, stores all previous and current versions. Used for evidential/audit trail and non-repudiation of content.
Special behaviors: Not visible in end-user listings—used for admin/forensics, supports complete content versioning.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description:
Primary Key - Implements unique snapshot identity (snapshot pattern, best practice for audit).

Uniquely identifies versions of thread content for traceability.

foreignFields.name: thread_id
foreignFields.description:
Parent thread's {@link threads.id} - Implements snapshot-thread association (requirement: snapshot versioning).

References the original thread. For example, all edits to a thread result in new snapshot records linked to this.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description:
Snapshot title - Implements versioned tracking of the thread title (requirement: snapshot content).

Title of the thread at this revision. For example, if a thread title changes, each version is preserved for audit/history.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description:
Snapshot content - Implements versioned content requirement (requirement: snapshot content).

Full body of the thread as it existed at this edit/history timestamp. For evidence and rollback.

plainFields.name: edited_by_user_id
plainFields.description:
Editor user reference - Tracks who edited thread (requirement: moderator/content editing, traceable history).

References user who made this revision; nullable for system-automated edits. For example, a moderator editing an abusive post.

plainFields.name: edit_reason
plainFields.description:
Edit reason - Documents reason for content change (requirement: moderation audit, forensic traceability).

Optional free-text field stating why edit was made (e.g. 'typo fix', 'policy violation edit'). Essential for accountability and audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Snapshot creation timestamp - Implements audit trail for this version (requirement: history).

Datetime when this snapshot/version was created. Needed for version ordering and chronology.

models.name: mv_thread_last_snapshots
models.description:
Materialized view: latest thread snapshots - This implements performance optimization and evidence-retrieval for thread versioning (best practice from BBS patterns).

Holds the latest snapshot for each thread as a fast lookup. 
For example, retrieving the current visible content for each thread in listing queries.

Key relationships: Linked to both threads and thread_snapshots, forms a fast bridge for getting the latest version for reads and forensic batch operations.
Special behaviors: Read-only, automatically updated on thread edit, always in sync with most recent snapshot (enforced at DB layer or via scheduled job).

primaryField.name: thread_id
primaryField.description:
Materialized view key - Thread identity, links to original thread.

One record per thread per materialized view pattern.

foreignFields.name: thread_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description:
Snapshot reference {@link thread_snapshots.id} - Implements last-snapshot linkage.

References the latest snapshot per thread. For fast reading of the newest visible content.

models.name: comments
models.description:
Comment entity - This implements the nested discussion and moderation requirement from the requirements document (Sections 2.2, 5.1, 5.3, and 6). 

Comments support both flat and hierarchical threading as replies under either a thread or another comment, enabling robust, structured conversation. For example, users can reply either to a thread directly or reply to another user's comment, forming discussion trees.

Key relationships: references threads, parent comments (for nesting), and users (authors). Comments relate to moderation actions, can be upvoted/downvoted, and have status tracking (active/removed).
Special behaviors: replies are recursively linked via parent_id, only registered users can post; moderated removal is soft-delete; all changes are auditable.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each comment instance.

foreignFields.name: thread_id
foreignFields.description: Parent thread's {@link threads.id} - Associates this comment directly with the thread it belongs to. If nested, parent_id links to another comment instead. Implements Section 5.3 'includes' relationship.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment's {@link comments.id} - For threaded replies, this links to the comment being replied to. Null for top-level (direct to thread) comments. Implements nested reply structure (Section 5.3, Section 2.2).

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Author's {@link users.id} - The user who wrote this comment. Implements Section 2.2 and 6 (user association for permissions, audit, and moderation).

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Body content of the comment - Implements the requirement of user-contributed discussion content. For example, a user's post, reply, or follow-up in a thread. No HTML limitations detailed, treat as rich text.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for creation - Implements the audit trail and reply order requirement (Section 6.5). For example, used for chronological sorting of comments.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp - Implements audit/change tracking for edits (Section 6.5). Allows users to update their own posts, and moderators to track all changes.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Status flag - Implements business rule for comment state (active/removed). For example, 'active' for visible comments, 'removed' for moderated/hidden. Used by moderation tools.

models.name: votes
models.description:
Vote record - This implements the requirement to allow users to express approval/disapproval for threads and comments, as referenced in the 'Upvote/Downvote System' and 'Vote (Optional)' features from section 4 and the entity in section 5 of the requirements analysis.

This model records each user's upvote or downvote on either a thread or comment, ensuring voting integrity and providing aggregate rating data to support better content curation and community ranking. For example, when a user upvotes or downvotes a thread or comment, a single record will be created or updated here.

Key relationships: Each vote is associated with exactly one user and either a thread or a comment (never both), both enforced by foreign keys. Strict uniqueness is enforced so each user can vote only once per target (thread or comment).
Special behaviors: Only registered users can vote (enforced by foreign key), and only one vote per user per content item is allowed. Votes can be updated (up->downvote or vice versa but not duplicated).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each vote record for tracking per-user voting activity. Ensures robust auditing and vote traceability (requirement: voting/audit trail).

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Voting user's {@link users.id} - Implements user association for each vote. Ensures only valid, registered users can cast a vote. For example, 'user_id' links each record to a registered account for auditability and permissions enforcement.

foreignFields.name: thread_id
foreignFields.description: Voted thread's {@link threads.id} - Target thread for this vote. Only one of thread_id or comment_id is set per record. For example, this links the vote to a discussion thread (not a comment). Required for upvoting/downvoting threads (not comments).

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: Voted comment's {@link comments.id} - Target comment for this vote. Only one of thread_id or comment_id is set per record. For example, this links the vote to a specific comment (not a thread). Required for upvoting/downvoting comments (not threads).

plainFields.name: vote_type
plainFields.description: Type of vote - Implements tracking of whether this is an upvote or downvote. For example, 'upvote'/'downvote', required for score calculation. Values constrained by application layer to two allowed types (requirement: explicit rating state for aggregation and display).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of vote creation - Implements audit and voting recency requirements. Business meaning: Tracks when a user cast a vote for time-based analytics; for example, detects recent activity spikes or prevents vote spam. Always set on insert.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update - Implements audit requirement and allows detection/moderation of changed votes. Business meaning: Provides an up-to-date modification time, e.g., if a user changes their vote. Set to current time on update.

models.name: moderation_actions
models.description:
Moderation Action entity - This implements the moderation logging and enforcement requirement from the requirement analysis (see Section 5: 'Moderation Action') and Section 6 (Business Rules 6.3). 

Business explanation: Records every administrative or moderation action (e.g., user bans, content removals, edits, category changes) to ensure accountability and transparency. For example, when a moderator deletes a comment for violating guidelines, an entry is made here. Used for future audits, appeals, and compliance needs.

Key relationships: Links to the moderator performing the action (references 'users' table), and references the moderation 'target': either a user, thread, or comment (polymorphic target).
Special behaviors: Always stores timestamp and action type, requires reference to at least one valid target, and logs reason for action; essential for audit trails and dispute resolution.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each moderation action.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator performing the action - links to {@link users.id}. Ensures only authorized accounts log moderation actions.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description:
Target type of the moderation action - Implements the moderation target entity (requirement aspect). 

Business meaning: Indicates what kind of entity was acted on ('user', 'thread', or 'comment').
Constraints: Allowed values are 'user', 'thread', or 'comment' (should be validated at business logic layer).

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description:
Target entity id - Implements linkage to the specific action target as per requirement. 

Holds the UUID of the user, thread, or comment being moderated.
Example: For a comment deletion, this holds the comment's id.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description:
Type of moderation action - Implements the enforcement action aspect from Section 6.3. 

Describes what action was taken (e.g., 'remove', 'ban', 'warn', 'edit'). For example, 'ban' if a user is banned.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description:
Reason for the moderation action - Implements the audit trail/business rules requirement. 

Explains why action was taken (e.g., 'hate speech policy', 'spam', etc). Used for transparency and review.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when action was performed - Implements audit-trail and accountability requirement. 

Business meaning: When the moderation action occurred. Used for chronological logs and compliance tracking.
